claim_under_test: evidence/audit/mixed-radix-bijection-v1's claim (bijection_holds_all_universes: true, acceptance_all_perfect: true; prose: 'proves the index<->tuple map is a BIJECTION ... surjective => no silent loss') constitutes independent corroboration that Cartesian enumeration reports every solved and infeasible combination without silent loss or ambiguity, as cited approvingly in docs/mission.md's T-06 Known Contradictions entry ('the module's own documented mixed-radix unranking').
finding: Universe A and universe B are ACCOUNTING-EQUIVALENT (identical sorted_axis_keys, identical radices, identical place_weights, identical cartesian_total_product=4, identical derived_infeasible_count=1, identical derived_solved_count=3 -- accounting_output_equal_a_vs_b=true, reproducing T-06's 'receipt_bytes_equal=true' finding at the oracle level) and EACH INDIVIDUALLY PASSES EVERY ACCEPTANCE METRIC AND FAILCLOSED PROBE THE SHIPPED mixed-radix-bijection-v1 ORACLE COMPUTES (both_universes_individually_pass_oracle_acceptance=true: bijection_roundtrip/injective/surjective/value_tuple_bijection all true for A alone and for B alone). Yet the declared infeasible index 1 decodes to ('IPDA','DGEBF') under A and ('TETA','DGEBF') under B -- representation_invariant_decode_a_vs_b=false -- reproducing T-06's exact counterexample bit-for-bit via the oracle's own published algorithm. The negative control (universe C, hardener order UNCHANGED from A) decodes identically to A (representation_invariant_decode_a_vs_c_negative_control=true), confirming the instability is caused specifically by the axis-value reordering and not by the harness. The mixed-radix-bijection-v1 oracle's acceptance vocabulary (10 per-universe rate fields plus 9 failclosed_probes, all read from run_mixed_radix_bijection.py) contains no field that is ever computed across two representations of what the runtime treats as 'the same' universe -- every metric is a property of ONE axes dict in isolation. It is therefore structurally incapable of detecting the representation-order defect T-06 already proved live in the Rust runtime, and would report 'acceptance_all_perfect: true' on BOTH universe A and universe B if either were substituted for a fixture entry, exactly as it does today. The receipt's claim to establish that the index<->tuple map is loss-free and duplication-free is true only within a single fixed representation; it does not and cannot establish representation-invariant identity, which is the specific property T-06 disproved and which docs/mission.md cites this oracle in connection with.

prior_finding_reproduced_as_input.quoted: the same declared infeasible index resolves to two different physical axis-value tuples across two accounting-equivalent (byte-identical-output) representations of 'the same' universe

refutation_criterion_verbatim: If two accounting-equivalent representations of the same declared universe (identical axis_cardinalities / cartesian_total / solved / infeasible counts under the oracle's own metrics) decode a shared declared infeasible index to two different physical value tuples, AND the mixed-radix-bijection-v1 oracle's acceptance_all_perfect / bijection_holds_all_universes metrics and 9 failclosed_probes do not flag either representation as failing, then the oracle's claim to certify 'no silent loss' / 'no silent duplication' for the Cartesian-accounting claim is incomplete: it does not cover, and cannot detect, the representation-order identity-instability defect class already proven live by T-06.
